fixes.explanation: Right on, baker. The LORD says, “I will put My law in their minds and inscribe it on their hearts.” Not just somewhere they have to go look at it. It goes inside them.

A scroll for everyone would be handy, friend. But the verse gives a different reason. The LORD says no longer will each man teach his neighbor or his brother to know Him, because “they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest…” No scroll is mentioned.

Signs are a big deal in the Bible, so I see where that came from. But this verse doesn't say signs. The LORD says no longer will each man teach his neighbor or his brother to know Him, because “they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest…” The reason is simply that they will know Him.
Close, but the statement is false, baker, and here's what the LORD says. “For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more.” He forgives, and He remembers their sins no more.

Earlier, the LORD did say they broke the old covenant (Jeremiah 31:32), so I see the connection you made. But this verse puts it a different way. The LORD says, “Only if this fixed order departed from My presence…” That's the only condition He names for Israel's descendants to cease to be a nation before Him.

Reject is the word, baker. The LORD says, “Only if the heavens above could be measured and the foundations of the earth below searched out would I reject all of Israel’s descendants because of all they have done…” Measuring the heavens, and I couldn't even measure a cup of flour right on my first day.

Gathering is a nice word, and it's good news, but it isn't what this verse says. The LORD says He would “…reject all of Israel’s descendants because of all they have done…” and only if the heavens could be measured and the earth's foundations searched out. Those are the conditions He names.

Bless would fit the mood, friend, but the LORD's word here is a different one. He says, “…would I reject all of Israel’s descendants because of all they have done…” The condition is measuring the heavens above and searching out the foundations of the earth below.

False, and the last line says it plain. The LORD says the whole valley of the dead bodies and ashes “…will be holy to the LORD.” Then He finishes with, “It will never again be uprooted or demolished.”
